pr_title: fix fqcr builtin/legacy connection plugins that accept extra variables
pr_body:
##### SUMMARY
Fixes #78566

* fix builtin/legacy connection plugins that accept extra variables when using the fqcr

* add a test for winrm extra vars

I checked 2.9 to see if there were any migrated connection plugins using this. `vmware_tools` sets allow_extras to True, but never appears to have used extra vars so I just fixed it for builtin/legacy. Plugins in collections can use config to get specific variables.

##### ISSUE TYPE
<!--- Pick one below and delete the rest -->
- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME
connection plugins

issue_context.title: Extra variables are ignored if using the FQCN of a builtin connection plugin
issue_context.body:
### Summary

When setting an builtin connection plugin using the variable `ansible_connection` with the FQCN (e.g. `ansible.builtin.winrm`) the extra variables are ignored.  

In my example I use the `winrm` connection plugin to connect to a Windows host with a self-signed certificate. So I need to set the variable `ansible_winrm_server_cert_validation` to `ignore`.  

It seems, that the name of the plugin is calculated wrong when using the FQCN for an builtin connection plugin.  
If I add an verbose output in [./lib/ansible/executor/task_executor.py](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/executor/task_executor.py) on line 1053 (`display.vv(f'CONNECTION LOAD_NAME: {self._connection._load_name}')`) the following is returned:

```
CONNECTION LOAD_NAME: ansible_collections.ansible.builtin.plugins.connection.winrm
```

As a result the extra variables with the prefix `ansible_winrm_` are ignored.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

winrm

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version
ansible [core 2.13.3]
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/my_user/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']

  ansible collection location = /home/my_user/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /home/my_user/.local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.8.10 (default, Jun 22 2022, 20:18:18) [GCC 9.4.0]
  jinja version = 3.1.2
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
# if using a version older than ansible-core 2.12 you should omit the '-t all'
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all
```


### OS / Environment

Ubuntu 20.04.4 LTS

### Steps to Reproduce

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
**Sample playbook:**
```yaml
---
- name: Test WinRM Connection
  hosts: windows-host
  gather_facts: false
  vars:
    ansible_connection: ansible.builtin.winrm
    ansible_host: "172.168.1.24"
    ansible_winrm_user: "UserOfMachine"
    ansible_winrm_password: "SuperSecurePa$$w0rd"
    ansible_winrm_server_cert_validation: ignore
    ansible_winrm_transport: basic

  tasks:
    - name: Set connection facts

    - name: Get C:\
      ansible.windows.win_powershell:
        script: Get-ChildItem C:\
...
```

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Have a Windows Server setup with a WinRM HTTPS listener and a self signed certificate
2. Run the playbook using `ansible-playbook -i inventory main.yml`

### Expected Results

I expected, that the task *Get C:\* returns the content of the windows-host's C:\ drive. This indicated that the winrm connection works with self signed certificates.

The name of the plugins matching the vars was the method pre Ansible 2.9, once we split into collections the 'names in documentation' are the ones used, so load_name there is for display, not variable matching. 

Now we use the  Config manager's `get_plugin_vars` method, which goes through each configuration entry (created when the plugin is loaded from reading the `DOCUMENTATION.options`). 

The mismatch might happen when we 'load' vs 'read' the options as the name might be taken from the 'base' and not match the `_load_name` as the connection plugins are preloaded (depending on path followed to load that particular plugin).
`get_url` is also getting the `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` error on MacOS `13.1 (22C65)`
